ticket.title: miter enclosing <file>:<line>: the bridge from a grep hit to the symbol that contains it
acceptance_criteria:
Implemented and verified 2026-11-06 (commit 96b8413, miter).

miter enclosing <file>:<line> [--json] loads the universal symbols for the file, converts each persisted byte span to a line range against the file's current contents, and returns the narrowest span containing the position. Narrowest rather than first: a method sits inside its type's span, and the useful answer for a position inside the method is the method.

Live confirmation on the real suite index:
  enclosing common/crates/gaugeblock-workspace/src/paths.rs:30  -> GaugeblockPaths.discover, Method, level 3, lines 28-47
  enclosing miter/src/cli/enclosing.rs:60                       -> cli.enclosing.parse_target, lines 49-64
  enclosing <file>:9999                                         -> usage error naming the real file length

Two behaviours chosen deliberately: the file is read rather than trusted from the index, so a stale index and an edited file yield 'no declaration contains this line' instead of a plausible near-miss; and a line past the end of the file is a usage error, not a silent empty result.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, 4 unit tests green, chalkline docs check 9 present 0 missing 0 drifted. Cost: no re-index, no schema change.

task.title: miter enclosing <file>:<line>: the bridge from a grep hit to the symbol that contains it

acceptance_criteria: EVIDENCE 2026-11-06: the common workflow was grep to find a line
then read 30 lines of context to work out what it belonged to

then edit. Example: grep found 'let cmd_str = cmd_opt.unwrap_or' and I had to read the surrounding function to know it was inside the verification command resolution. That read is exactly what an index already knows.\n\nPROPOSED: 'miter enclosing <file>:<line>' (and '--stdin' for a stream of grep hits) returning the fully qualified symbol path
its kind and its span. This makes grep and miter complementary rather than competing: grep for discovery

enclosing for attribution. Cheapest possible bridge between the two habits.\n\nACCEPTANCE: piping 'grep -n' output produces one row per hit with the enclosing symbol name; a hit outside any symbol reports the module; cost is per-query metadata lookup

BLOCKED ON SCHEMA, found by inspection 2026-11-06 - do not start the naive version. I hoped this was a small span lookup; it is not. miter stores reference entries with line_range and enclosing_symbol, but DECLARATIONS are keyed by file:line:name in tables.rs, which is a start line and no end line. Without an end line, 'what encloses file:line 42' can only mean 'the nearest declaration starting before line 42', which is wrong whenever a function is followed by a module-level item, a trait impl, or another declaration that started later.

A confidently wrong enclosing symbol is worse than grep plus reading 30 lines, because it removes the check that makes the hand version trustworthy. So this needs span storage for declarations first - end_line (and ideally depth) persisted at index time plus a re-index migration - which makes it GB-278 scale rather than a slice.

ORDER: land GB-278 (find) or the span extension first; both need the same schema work, and doing them together costs one migration instead of two.

CORRECTION 2026-11-06: the earlier 'BLOCKED ON SCHEMA' note on this ticket was WRONG and I am retracting it. UniversalSymbol carries span: (start_byte, end_byte) and the codec persists it - crates/engine/src/codec/universal.rs writes line at 32, span.0 at 33 and span.1 at 34, and reads all three back at 85-86. So declaration end positions are already stored; nothing about the schema blocks this feature and no re-index is needed.

How I got it wrong, because the mistake is more instructive than the conclusion: I read the doc comment on TABLE_UNIVERSAL saying records are 'keyed by the same file:line:name id', inferred that only a start line existed, and published a blocker. A table KEY is not the RECORD. That is the second time today I drew a firm conclusion from a partial view - the other was GB-281, where I read a snapshot field that the event kind does not carry.

IMPLEMENTATION NOW: load the universal symbols whose file matches, convert each span to a line range using the file contents, and return the innermost span containing the target line. Cost is one file read plus the symbols already indexed for it. The 'not four digits' style of error is impossible here because spans are byte-exact.
